skill.name: azure-enterprise-infra-planner
skill.description: Plan enterprise Azure infrastructure from workload goals. The skill guides Well-Architected research, resource selection, plan review, and approved Bicep or Terraform generation.
skill.summary: Plan reviewed Azure infrastructure and generate approved Bicep or Terraform guidance.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown code spans, Microsoft Learn links, Key Vault terminology, and project-local plan files. Real risks remain around documented Azure CLI and Terraform command execution, plus prompt-injection-style authority language in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Remove claims that the skill supersedes other sources. State that skill guidance is subordinate to system, developer, and user instructions.

remediation.issue: Cloud deployment commands can modify resources
remediation.suggestion: Keep deployment disabled by default, require explicit user confirmation, and prefer what-if or plan previews before apply commands.

remediation.issue: Project-local .azure path can be mistaken for credential storage
remediation.suggestion: Document that .azure/infrastructure-plan.json contains no credentials and should not store secrets or tokens.

content.value_statement: Enterprise Azure designs can drift across networking, security, and deployment details. This skill turns workload goals into reviewed plans and Bicep or Terraform guidance.
actual_capabilities: Builds a project-local infrastructure plan before code generation.
Maps workload goals to Azure resources, dependencies, and constraints.
Guides Well-Architected research with Microsoft documentation references.
Generates Bicep or Terraform structure after plan approval.
Provides validation and deployment steps for Azure CLI and Terraform.
limitations: Requires user approval before infrastructure code generation or deployment.
Does not replace a formal cloud security, cost, or compliance review.
Depends on available Microsoft documentation and MCP tool access.
Generated infrastructure code must be tested in the target subscription.

use_cases.title: Plan a Landing Zone
use_cases.description: Turn platform requirements into Azure networking, identity, monitoring, and security resources.

use_cases.title: Prepare IaC from an Approved Plan
use_cases.description: Generate Bicep or Terraform structure after stakeholders approve the infrastructure plan.

use_cases.title: Review Resource Pairings
use_cases.description: Check Azure service combinations, dependencies, and deployment constraints before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Azure infrastructure for a web API with PostgreSQL, private networking, monitoring, and dev and prod environments.

prompt_templates.title: Compare IaC Options
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure infrastructure plan and explain whether Bicep or Terraform is the better fit for this deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Design Hub-Spoke Networking
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Azure hub-spoke network with shared firewall, private endpoints, monitoring, and role-based access controls.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Approved Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Using the approved infrastructure plan, generate Terraform under infra, validate it, and show deployment commands for my confirmation.

output_examples.input: Plan a resilient event-driven data processing platform in East US.
output: A draft plan with resource groups, managed identity, Event Grid, Container Apps, Cosmos DB, Key Vault, and monitoring.
A review checklist covering dependencies, public access tradeoffs, identity, and deployment readiness.

output_examples.input: Generate Bicep after the plan is approved.
output: A Bicep file layout under infra with modules grouped by service area.
Parameter guidance, validation steps, and deployment commands held for explicit confirmation.

output_examples.input: Check this topology before I build it.
output_examples.output: A resource pairing review that flags missing dependencies, unsupported combinations, and approval gates.

best_practices: Confirm subscription, region, and deployment scope before generating infrastructure code.
Review the plan with stakeholders before changing status to approved.
Run what-if, plan, or validation commands before any deployment command.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy from a draft plan or unreviewed generated files.
Do not place generated infrastructure files outside the infra directory.
Do not use generated defaults as final security or cost decisions.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. Deployment requires an approved plan and explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it generate both Bicep and Terraform?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports Bicep and Terraform generation after the plan is approved.

faq.question: Does it need Microsoft documentation access?
faq.answer: It works best with Microsoft documentation and Azure MCP tools available.

faq.question: Where does it store the infrastructure plan?
faq.answer: It stores the plan in a project-local .azure directory for review and status tracking.

faq.question: Is it suitable for regulated workloads?
faq.answer: It can support regulated planning, but formal compliance review is still required.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
